prompt.en: Would you rather fight an infection with an antibiotic that kills the bacteria, or a jammer that stops them cooperating? Write your view first.

viewpoints.en: Killing is decisive and proven. A jammer leaves the bacteria alive for the body to deal with, and a weak patient might not manage.
Killing selects hard for resistance: any survivor is a survivor of the drug, from Book VIII. A jammer that only silences may select less strongly, because a deaf bacterium still lives and divides.
Both together. Silence the biofilm first so the antibiotic can reach the cells, then kill. Most real strategies against biofilms are combinations.
There is no settled answer. The trials are running now.

image.alt: Two paths to fighting an infection, one a direct strike killing bacteria and one a quiet jammer silencing their communication, side by side and unresolved.
